chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded these verses to descend to the earth, they clung to the Throne and said: 'O Lord, to where are You causing us to descend? To the people of errors and sins?'

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to them to descend: 'By My Might and My Majesty! No one from the Progeny of Muhammad and their Shias will recite you at the end of what I have imposed upon him from the prescribed [prayers] in every day, except that I will look at him with My Hidden Eye in every day with seventy glances, fulfilling for him in every glance seventy needs, and accepting him despite whatever he is in from disobediences.'
And these are: the Mother of the Book, and the Verse of the Throne, and the Verse of Dominion.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit for the Ahl al-Bayt and their followers when reciting specific Quranic verses after daily prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the metaphysical reverence of Quranic verses, personifying them as hesitant to descend among sinners until God guarantees their special protection for the Ahl al-Bayt and their Shias. It establishes a unique spiritual mechanism where reciting these specific verses after obligatory prayers triggers seventy divine glances, each fulfilling a need, thereby ensuring acceptance despite lingering sins. This underscores the Shia theological emphasis on the intercessory and purifying power of the Quran through the lens of the Imams' lineage.
